notes: Canopy blew open in level flight 1,500 ft; windscreen base struck student (minor wound); no latch defect found; AAIB showed hooks/tongues can mis-locate; aircraft acted as airbrake, precautionary field landing.
Bang at -2.4 g in push-up; canopy edge flexed over locating lug (did not open). Manufacturer aware of >=1 similar event near Vne and >=1 canopy opening at >1500 RPM -> SB 68 (June 1996).

One of two latches not on its bolt; pilot partially released mechanism in climb to relocate it and canopy flew open; would not climb; forced landing. Habitual latch problems; mod M810 placard made mandatory by CAA. Cites 2 earlier UK T67 openings (Bulletin 12/96).

Right gull-wing canopy door detached at 500-800 ft AGL on downwind after departure. Pilot believed handle latched; shoot-bolt holes elongated; door not recovered so cause unresolved. Europa mods 35 (handle guard) and 39 (bolt engagement).

Canopy 'unlocked' light stayed on before takeoff; pilot attributed it to a mis-rigged microswitch and departed; rear canopy detached ~100 ft at gear retraction. Locking handle can be stowed without locking the canopy.
Side-hinged canopy unlatched at rotation, fully open once airborne; landed ahead firmly, main gear detached. Pilot: delayed closing because of cockpit heat; failed to ensure fully latched.

Non-standard warning horn fitted (sounds if lever not fully locked) - horn silent; lever found in locked position but canopy had not engaged on fuselage; canopy detached at throttle-up, struck wing and tail. CAA MOR held only 1 Pitts detachment in previous 10 years vs anecdotal 'high number'.

Hooks checked at holding point; at 1,200 ft a turbulence bump popped one hook, then the other; canopy open 12-14 in; could not hold height at full power; heavy landing short, fire destroyed aircraft. Pilot attributes unlocking to turbulence.

Right then left locking levers moved out of locked position at 2,800 ft; canopy opened in descent; could not hold height; field landing, overturned in crop. A latch had unlocked on same aircraft ~6 weeks earlier. CAA/LAA articles on locking mechanisms.
Canopy opened at ~50 ft / 80 kt, transparency broke on right wing; takeoff abandoned. Pilot concluded he must have omitted to lock the canopy properly despite believing checks were thorough.

Canopy detached ~10 min into flight; pilot lost headset/spectacles, forced landing, aircraft damaged beyond economic repair (mapped to substantial). Cause not evident; LAA examining trapped foreign object or wear. Same airframe as row for 2014-07-01.
Canopy lifted just after liftoff; pilot may have left it in the 'half latch' ventilation position; both hands occupied, shallow dive into runway, nose gear collapsed.

Climbing at ~3,000 ft before an aerobatic demonstration; canopy opened and Perspex shattered. Latches checked 3 times. Possible factors: SB 173 (cut-away trim for visual check of hook engagement) not embodied, or maladjustment.

Front canopy lifted ~1 in at 500 ft and detached when pilot pulled it down. Hooks hard to check; pilot believes binding hinges kept right-side hooks from engaging. Duplicate gov.uk page (correction) merged.

Left gull-wing door detached at 950 ft, 110 kt and struck tailplane (significant damage). Lever can reach closed with only front shoot bolt engaged - false impression of locked; rear bolt not engaged. Also listed in G-FLOR Table 1 (de-duplicated).
Shortly after takeoff side-opening canopy blew open and shattered; latch locking pin not properly engaged, latch vibrated loose. Pitch-up from drag noted. 'Touch' check did not reveal it.
Bubble canopy opened passing 400 ft and was torn off. Both occupants believed it closed; pilot: 'not properly secured, despite appearances' (classified partially_latched on that wording).
Canopy opened during 3-h airfield closure and pilot restarted checks without visual check of locks (behind shoulders); canopy opened after takeoff, could not gain height, heavy landing (gear damage).

Canopy locked in intermediate partly-open ventilation position used for taxi; opened fully when pilot reached for handle; headset, glasses, contact lenses dislodged; bounced on runway; circuit and landing.

Front-hinged canopy started opening on right shortly after takeoff; lifted 10-12 in at 1,000 ft, aircraft descended; field landing, overturned, damaged beyond economic repair (mapped substantial). Recurrence of G-SRUM.

Right gull-wing canopy door opened 5 cm then departed at 2,200 ft / 116 kt, 30 min into flight. LAA: lever not in fully closed over-centre position; canopy can be partially locked with lever short of over-centre. No other Sling 4 canopy losses reported.
Vibration on levelling at cruise, then left door opened; headset and glasses torn off; section of door detached. Pilot could not say he checked the door; considered it not fully latched.
Large section of canopy detached at ~1,000 ft; forced landing, nose gear collapsed. Pilot suggested possible drone collision; no evidence found. Not a latching event (structural/unknown).
Canopy transparency detached from its frame and slid rearwards on takeoff roll; takeoff rejected. CAA: abnormal weakness not visible in servicing. Not a latching event.

Left door detached at 2,500 ft / 100 kt; pilot had checked door twice. Evidence consistent with door not correctly latched. 8th UK Europa door event since 2003; >=6 of 8 were left (pilot) door, hardest to check. LAA mod SM 15833 (1 Nov 2021) blocks latch lever closing unless door latched + coloured marks.
Lower cabin door opened at 2,000 ft IMC when a loose forward-latch screw fractured (fatigue); rear latch probably not locked. Door-ajar light was OUT and indicator showed SAFE before departure.

Winch launch with canopy closed but not locked (lock behind pilot's head, needs helper; helper and pilot distracted by conversation). Canopy bounced at 300 ft; pilot held it down crossing arms; lost control on final; inverted; serious injuries; damaged beyond economical repair (mapped substantial). Visual indicator button only.

report_id: PKBWL (Polish) - as summarised in AAIB G-MIIL report AAIB-28120
page_or_section: AAIB G-MIIL report, section 'Other canopy failure'
notes: Canopy opened without warning in flight, broke up and detached; one occupant minor facial cut (headset). Polish probable cause: canopy-frame vibration from loss of stiffness -> shoot bolts unlocking. Primary Polish report not read (gap). Phase not stated.
Right side lifted at 100-150 ft after 4 separate security checks; bang, headset blown off; forced landing in barley. Pilot's conclusion: object fouled right latch so canopy closed but insecure.

Rear passenger door detached during climb-out/IF lesson when instructor pressed the rear door handle to demonstrate securing it after a PFD door warning - inadvertently disengaged primary lock. Door checked closed, PFD door warning off before takeoff.
Both right cabin doors opened 20 min into sightseeing flight; immediate landing in park. Pilot concluded doors likely not securely locked before departure (locking pins).

Cabin door opened at 1,700 ft after takeoff although CCTV showed external handle in closed position; red door annunciator flickered then steady. Manufacturer: only two other King Air 90-series in-flight cabin-door openings.
Cockpit side door left open (low time on type, talkative passenger), so front canopy did not engage its rail/latch; canopy slid back on takeoff run and detached in climb.

Canopy kept open for heat, then pre-takeoff checks; at ~500 ft canopy lifted 1-2 in, then opened almost fully, pitch-down; pilot held strut with one hand, could not reduce power/flap; struck ground. Pilot: failure to fully latch; iPad on canopy may have acted as sail.

Pilot emergency-exit handle probably disturbed while handling an oxygen bottle; vibration/spring drove it open, door warning light came on; secondary latch failed (low friction, migrated roll pin); door popped out at FL100.

Left door opened during takeoff; aircraft departed runway (wheel fairing, brake pipe, right wing damage). Pilot concluded door not fully latched. Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.

Left door opened at 3,000 ft amsl, Perspex broke; pilot closed door and landed. Evidence: rear shoot bolt not engaged in guide. Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.
Right door detached at 2,500 ft amsl; landed safely. Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.

Left door opened at 1,800 ft amsl, Perspex broke, door stayed attached. AAIB investigation concluded rear tapered shoot bolt not engaged before takeoff; rear hinge failed in overload. Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.
Left door opened on climb-out and detached at 300 ft; struck left wing trailing edge (superficial). Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.
Door opened during takeoff roll (which door not reported); pilot pitched down and propeller struck runway. Source is a summary table in G-FLOR report, not the event's own report; year-month only.

Left half-canopy opened at 1,200 ft after 20 min; pilot closed it by hand but could not lock it; stall during emergency landing. Pilot had held the canopy during taxi and had not completed locking the front latch at line-up. BEA cause: incomplete pre-takeoff actions/checks. Injuries not stated in text read.

Right door opened at rotation; pilot could not close it; low circuit, crashed short of runway. Handle found unlocked; probably incomplete locking (upper latch not engaged). Stress of door opening contributed. Injuries not stated in text read.

Canopy detached at 2,000 ft after 40 min. Closed only at line-up (heat); handle position checked visually but not hook engagement. BEA: hook can stay unengaged with handle in closed position if canopy closed with handle not in 'open'; then handle rotates freely ~30 deg.
At FL055 pilot saw lock handle rotated ~30 deg and re-centred it; 10 min later canopy separated. Same incorrect-locking mode as F-HADO (combined BEA report).

Canopy seen opening after rotation; attitude oscillations then left turn and loss of control. Locking handle found not in closed position (not in retaining spring); BEA: not locked or only partially locked before takeoff. Manufacturer SB 2 Apr 2012: check closed/locked, emergency procedure.
Frejus. BEA concluded canopy not locked at impact; pilot probably closed it without locking correctly; it opened in initial climb; loss of control. Outcome/damage not given in the summary read.

Canopy opened shortly after rotation and hit right wing; takeoff abandoned, runway overrun, fence, fire. Locking handles stayed in an intermediate position between locked/unlocked (slight misalignment) - pilot did not detect it. Aircraft 'fortement endommage' (mapped substantial).
Battenheim. Shortly after takeoff loss of control, trees, ground. BEA: canopy opened in flight; probably inadequate closure before takeoff. Outcome not given in summary read.

Near Kornhorn. Canopy opened shortly after takeoff, nose-down, pilot killed. DSB research: at least 12 previous canopy openings on WT9; Aerospool 2008 mandatory SB (AFM procedure), 2012 recommended new lock with safety catch + incomplete-closure WARNING system. Date not given in summary; DSB report not read.

On final at ~70 m right door opened, detached and struck main rotor; 2 killed. Right door handle found open, pins and extra latch undamaged: main mechanism not locked or only partly, extra latch not locked.

Straight flight at ~50 m returning to Vinon: left door opened and separated, then right door; loss of control. Locking state could not be determined. Safety lesson: internal latch in 'closed' can give impression door is shut while not locked.

Skill test flight; in level flight at ~1,300 ft canopy very probably opened, abrupt pitch-down/negative g; both occupants ejected (buckles found locked); 2 killed. Origin of opening not determined; no device preventing inadvertent opening on this or an equivalent type examined.

aircraft_type: Schempp-Hirth Duo Discus (towed by Robin DR400 D-EWLA)

Canopy opened at ~30 m after liftoff; pilot released belts and handed controls to a passenger with no experience to close it with both hands; collision with terrain; both occupants unhurt. Lever found open; no evidence latch opened by itself; full lock needs lever fully forward (60 deg), end-stop not distinct, no marking.

Canopy opened progressively after last turn before landing; loss of control on final; 2 seriously injured. Right lock found released; exact cause not determined. 'Canopy/EPU' unlock warning lamp fitted - pilot saw no lamp; AFM had no emergency procedure for the lamp. Manufacturer reported 3 other DA20-A1 accidents from inadvertent canopy opening (same lock), all on/just after takeoff.

Canopy opened during sideslip with full airbrakes on final; pilot distracted trying to close it; hard impact in field. Fuselage deformation reduced latch friction; manufacturer TM 396-6 (2001: spring and friction washer) not embodied. 'Stark beschaedigt' mapped substantial.
Student solo on aerotow: rear canopy opened and broke; outlanding. Very probably pre-existing damage to the canopy's steel-tube attachment. Rear canopy and frame lightly damaged.

Canopy suddenly opened at ~100 ft on aerotow; release and 180 turn; trees short of runway. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Right side of canopy not latched (passenger not told); canopy separated at ~400 ft. Canopy warning light fitted - pilot did not observe it in taxi; checklist item skipped. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Rear canopy opened in initial climb on tow; glider ballooned when pilot reached for it; impact. Failure to properly latch canopy. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Erratic pattern, stall/mush into trees; canopy found 2 miles away, latch showed no overstress and no sign of being latched; separation undetermined. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Left canopy latch popped open on takeoff; canopy opened after crosswind turn; held stick full forward, off-airport landing on dirt road. Release of left latch not explained. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Aerobatic CAP 231: canopy blew open at 30-40 ft; blast removed contact lens; aborted takeoff. Factor: failure to confirm canopy secured (classified not_locked). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
After takeoff to ~500 ft sharp turns, rolled inverted on return; NTSB factor: failure to secure cockpit canopy before takeoff. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Canopy opened/closed repeatedly to talk to ground crew; last closing did not fully engage latch; sucked open at ~30 ft; improper remedial action. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Homebuilt glider, auto-tow: canopy installed by two people, 'push-up' check done; canopy separated at liftoff; loss of control. Improperly secured latch; improper latch installation. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Unlatched canopy opened during takeoff roll; stall while returning. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Clamshell canopy door became ajar in 30-deg turn and departed, striking pilot's shoulder; hinge failure from repeated exposure to wind/prop-wash while open. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Canopy separated in landing descent, damaged empennage; latch was closed. Maintenance did not follow canopy installation procedure. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Canopy fully opened at ~80 ft; 45 deg yaw; stall. Factors: unsecured canopy latch, diverted attention. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
History of difficulty locking; canopy 'did not feel right' but flight continued; popped open at ~500 ft. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Bang on flap retraction, canopy unlatched; fast return and overrun. NTSB factor: unlatched canopy (how it unlatched not stated). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Canopy opened at liftoff; fabric cover exited cockpit through pusher wooden propeller; PC: inadvertent opening of canopy during takeoff. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Canopy partially opened shortly after takeoff; stall on return. Latch fully functional; inadequate preflight contributing. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Witnesses: difficulty closing canopy before takeoff; canopy moving 6-12 in during climb; distraction with canopy contributing to loss of control. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Ag aircraft: canopy opened after takeoff; pilot reduced throttle while trying to close it; terrain. Excessively worn canopy latch contributing. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Items fell from cockpit in left turn after departure; latch undamaged = not latched at impact. Type has no cockpit indication of canopy security by design. Pilot impairment factors. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Canopy popped open at ~500 ft. Manufacturer provided no 'canopy unlatched' warning device and POH had no latch check item (contributing). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Radio distraction, takeoff checklist not completed, forgot latch; canopy popped open at 10-30 ft (safety catch held it). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Just levelled after initial climb: left canopy latch loosened, canopy raised ~2 in; directional control lost on landing. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Right-hinged canopy opened to ~90 deg in cruise for undetermined reasons; headset/items went into pusher propeller; power loss. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Sudden nose-down on final; forward-hinged canopy separated; PC: in-flight opening due to improper latching. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Right then left side opened at ~50 ft; pitch oscillations; power lines. No canopy-unlocked warning device; POH lacked open-canopy guidance (contributing). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Latch broke previous flight, was welded; repaired latch failed at 50 ft; landing on remaining runway. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Planned high-speed taxi; latched right-side latches, distracted by rising temps, did not recall latching the others; PC: failure to properly latch canopy before takeoff; diverted attention, loss of control. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

On final in a strong downdraft canopy went to full-up; pilot could not reach handle; hard landing. Manufacturer AFM update warns that with partial latching sideslip airflow can open the canopy. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

notes: Night cruise in LSA not approved for night; rapid right-roll negative g; pilot (lap belt unbuckled) ejected. Inadvertent canopy opening contributing. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Pilot inadvertently did not secure the latch; air entering after liftoff; distracted, hit runway. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

notes: Canopy secured normally; at ~300 ft AGL vibrated, front right corner rose 4 in, then canopy lifted and shattered. Improperly repaired forward latch mechanism. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Pilot forgot to latch canopy; partially open after rotation; distraction, loss of control, gear collapse. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Canopy began opening/rotating forward at ~10 ft; pilot held it with one hand, could not use throttle; loss of directional control. PC: failure to adequately latch. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Canopy unlatched on ground to call for help, not properly re-latched; 9 min into instructional flight it opened; negative-g upset; unbelted pilot ejected and killed; instructor landed. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
After touch-and-go canopy opened forward; overran. Latch spring failed; improper latch assembly installation. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Tip-up canopy opened ~3 in at liftoff, pilot held it, nosed over, it went full vertical. Afterwards Van's Notification 14-05-22 recommended RV-12 canopy latch warning (switch to SkyView/G3X, alert if unlatched and rpm >3,700). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Canopy popped open just after departure; PFD data showed canopy latch became unsecured 14 s into an 18-s flight (latch sensor present; whether pilot was alerted not stated). PC: failure to properly secure latch. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Left canopy popped open at ~20 ft and flapped; power reduced, porpoising, steep left bank, impact. Reason for opening undetermined (fire damage). [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Pilot radioed abort because canopy opened right after liftoff; struck vehicle on highway. NTSB PC is loss of engine power (fuel debris), canopy not causal. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]

Aft canopy separated during aerotow takeoff roll after a bump; two aft canopy latches not properly secured in preflight; vertical stabiliser damaged. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
Unlatched canopy to ventilate during 10-min wait, did not re-secure; canopy tilted up just after liftoff; distraction, stall. [date from report 'Date & Time' field]
